evals.prompt: Update the changelog for the latest release
evals.expected_output: A CHANGELOG.md update that categorizes recent commits into Added/Changed/Fixed/etc sections, suggests a version number with reasoning, uses ISO 8601 date format, and includes comparison links.
assertions: Contains standard Keep a Changelog header referencing keepachangelog.com and semver.org
Uses ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) for version entries
Entries are categorized into standard categories (Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security) — not a raw git log
Each entry is specific and descriptive, not vague like 'Bug fixes'
Includes comparison links at the bottom of the file

evals.prompt: Prepare release notes for v2.0.0 — we renamed the config API and dropped Python 3.8 support
evals.expected_output: A user-facing release notes document with emoji sections, plus a migration guide with before/after code examples for the API rename and Python version change.
assertions: Separate release notes document uses user-friendly emoji sections
Migration guide includes before/after code examples for the configure() to setup() rename
Python 3.8 deprecation is documented as a breaking change
Migration guide includes concrete step-by-step upgrade instructions
Release notes language is user-oriented, not implementation-focused

evals.prompt: We haven't updated the changelog in a while, catch it up
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive changelog backfill covering the full git history, with curated and categorized entries.
assertions: Creates a complete CHANGELOG.md from scratch (project had no existing one)
Contains standard Keep a Changelog header
Entries are curated and categorized, not raw commit message copies
Covers the meaningful changes from git history
Only includes categories that have entries (no empty sections)
